description: Per-device poll health from the 'diagnostics' measurement (written once a minute by logger.py). device tag values: meter, inverter, battery_dev2 (dongle device=2 power/temp), battery_dev4 (dongle device=4 BMS).

panels.title: Average read latency by device
panels.description: Mean latency over every completed read attempt in the minute, including failed/timed-out ones — rising latency is an early warning before outright failures.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "home")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "diagnostics" and r["_field"] == "avg_latency_ms")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: Successful reads / min by device
panels.description: Count of reads that returned usable data in each minute. Healthy: meter & inverter ~ their poll rate; battery_dev2 ~ 6/min (10 s poll); battery_dev4 ~ 1 every 5 min (300 s poll ⇒ 0 most minutes).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "home")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "diagnostics" and r["_field"] == "reads_ok")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: Failed reads / min by device
panels.description: Count of read attempts that raised (HTTP error, timeout, transport failure) in each minute. This is the primary dropout signal — spikes here mark the dongle/link falling over.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "home")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "diagnostics" and r["_field"] == "reads_fail")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: Deadband drops / min by device
panels.description: Samples the per-device deadband filter held back each minute. NOTE: the filter runs on the main loop's 3 Hz interpolated stream (~180 samples/min), NOT on raw reads — so this sits near ~180 for a healthy device regardless of its actual read rate, and falls toward 0 only during an outage (no readings to interpolate/drop). It measures logged-output compression, not read health — use the reads/latency panels for that. battery_dev4 is not deadband-filtered, so it stays at 0.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "home")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "diagnostics" and r["_field"] == "deadband_drops")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)

title: Device Diagnostics
